{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement (Kubient)

**Document:** Exhibit 10.14, Master Services Agreement, dated as of 5 February
**Reviewed for:** Customer (Client)
**Prepared by:** In-house counsel

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook. The commercial architecture is favourable to us on most of the terms we care about most: the arrangement is expressly non-exclusive, there is no non-compete, no minimum commitment, no MFN, no non-solicit and no audit right running against us; the vendor indemnity is broad and uncapped; ownership sits in the right direction (we retain our Content and Properties, and Kubient's ownership is confined to its own Auction Platform IP); the vendor's warranties run for the whole Term and are not swallowed by the "as is" disclaimer; assignment and termination for convenience are acceptable, the latter at the fallback.

Five items require attention. The single most serious is the **absence of any aggregate liability cap** — Section 7 excludes indirect and consequential damages but leaves our direct liability unlimited, which fails our fallback outright. Two further items sit in walk-away territory on our playbook: the **licence grant is expressly "revocable"** and excludes our affiliates and contractors with no path to add them, and there is **no insurance covenant at all** even though Kubient collects, stores and manages visitor data. In addition, the **auto-renewal** mechanic gives us only an effective 90-day exit window (fallback maximum is 60 days), and there is **no post-termination transition assistance or data return** obligation.

We recommend proceeding, subject to closing the liability cap, licence scope and insurance points before signature.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** | Preamble | No aggregate monetary cap anywhere; our direct liability is unlimited. Fails the fallback (mutual 12-month cap). |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | Preamble | At or above preferred position and uncapped; our own indemnity is broader than we prefer, noted only. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | Preamble | Correct direction of ownership; no express "Customer Data" sentence or deliverables licence-back, noted only. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | Preamble | Licence is expressly "revocable", non-transferable, and excludes affiliates and contractors. Walk-away territory. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | Preamble | Meets fallback and substantially the preferred position; no competitor restriction on Kubient, noted only. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | Preamble | Expressly non-exclusive; preferred position met. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties | Compliant | Preamble | No LDs, penalties, minimum fees or early-termination fees payable by us. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | Preamble | No non-compete or field-of-use covenant; Section 6 limits are ordinary acceptable-use terms. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant (fallback) | Preamble | 12-month Initial Term, then exit for any reason on 90 days' notice, no exit fee. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | **Deviation** | Preamble | Auto-renews for 1-year terms with only an effective 90-day exit window, exceeding the 60-day fallback maximum. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | **Missing** | Preamble | No data return in usable format, no deletion certification, no transition assistance. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | Preamble | No audit, inspection or verification right over us. Nothing to redline. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant (fallback) | Preamble | Delaware law, exclusive New York venue; AAA arbitration and one-year claims limitation noted, not walk-away. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | Preamble | No MFN or price-matching obligation on us. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | Preamble | Pure revenue share; no minimum spend, volume, take-or-pay or shortfall. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | Preamble | No non-solicit, no-hire or inducement restriction on us. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | Preamble | Warranties run for the Term; "as is" disclaimer is expressly subject to them. No stated re-performance remedy, noted only. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | Preamble | No insurance covenant despite Kubient collecting, storing and managing visitor data. Walk-away territory. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

Two findings sit in walk-away territory on our playbook and should not be conceded:

1. **Licence grant scope (LICENSE, high).** A licence revocable at the vendor's discretion, with affiliates and contractors excluded and no path to add them, is walk-away territory. Our redline deletes "revocable", extends the grant to affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, permits transfer to an M&A successor, and ties termination of the licence to Section 4.
2. **Vendor insurance (INSURANCE, low severity, walk-away in substance).** For a vendor processing personal data, the total absence of an insurance covenant is walk-away territory. We have inserted our standard CGL/E&O/cyber paragraph in the General Provisions, with E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M available as a fallback.

We also treat the **absence of any liability cap (LOL-CAP)** as a must-fix: it fails the fallback on a material term and leaves our direct exposure unlimited.

For completeness, two items were assessed and expressly do **not** reach walk-away territory: the mutual convenience-termination right and Kubient's retention of fees generated during the notice period (T4C), and the AAA arbitration clause, which is domestic rather than seated abroad (GOVLAW).

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Liability cap.** Send the redline adding a mutual aggregate cap to Section 7 at the greater of 12 months' amounts and USD 1,000,000, with indemnities, confidentiality/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement expressly outside the cap. Position as the playbook requirement; the 12-month mutual cap is our fallback.
2. **Licence grant.** Send the redline deleting "revocable", extending the licence to affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, permitting transfer to an M&A successor, and tying licence termination to Section 4. Flag the Section 6(a) third-party access consent gate as part of the same conversation.
3. **Insurance.** Insert the standard CGL/E&O/cyber paragraph into the General Provisions; hold E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M in reserve as the fallback.
4. **Transition and data return.** Insert Section 4(c)(v): up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates (90 days acceptable as fallback), data return in machine-readable form within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter.
5. **Auto-renewal.** Add an express 30-day non-renewal right to the auto-renewal sentence (60 days acceptable as fallback). The 12-month renewal length is acceptable and there is no price-uplift language to cap.
6. **Diligence items to close internally.** (a) Review each Exhibit on issuance for any minimum spend or volume commitment, which the body of the Agreement does not impose; (b) if bespoke deliverables become material, add an express Customer Data ownership sentence and a licence-back; (c) consider asking Kubient to align Sections 8 and 14(a) on a single forum, as a non-blocking request.

Please let us know if you would like the redlines circulated as a single mark-up or split between the must-fix items (1–3) and the remainder."}
